title: Polynomial-time pair-length check
statement: For all natural numbers $C$ and $e$, there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)^{e+1}$ steps and outputs a single bit. That bit is true exactly when the aligned pair parser returns components $(a,b)$ with $|b|\le C(|a|+1)^e$; it is false if parsing fails.
replaced:
For all constants $C$ and $e$ there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a
constant $c$ such that $M$ computes, within $c\,(n+1)^{e+1}$ steps on inputs
of length $n$, the one-bit function that on a word encoding the pair $(a,b)$
under the self-delimiting pair code outputs whether
$\abs{b} \le C\,(\abs{a}+1)^{e}$, and on any malformed word outputs $0$.
